deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes an argument started on the previous page. Let rho_i(u) be the decreasing 'singular numbers' of an operator u. In a Hilbert space these are the s-numbers. In the Banach-space setting of these notes they are probably defined through the norms of Lambda^n u; the neighbouring page uses exterior powers and Fredholm determinants.

Step 1 (previous page). Grothendieck has, for every r >= 0 and every n, the multiplicative Weyl/Horn-Fan type inequality prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(u+v)) <= prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(u)) prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(v)). In additive form this reads A(r) <= B(r), where A(r) = sum log(1+r rho_i(u+v)), B is the corresponding sum for u and v, and A(0) = B(0) = 0.

Step 2. Integrating by parts against -phi', with phi >= 0 decreasing, gives int phi A' <= int phi B'. Here A'(r) = sum rho_i/(1+r rho_i), where the previous page's transcription drops a rho in the numerator. Define f_phi(rho) = int_0^inf phi(r) rho/(1+r rho) dr = int_0^inf phi(s/rho) ds/(1+s). Then sum_{i<=n} f_phi(rho_i(u+v)) <= sum_{i<=n} [f_phi(rho_i(u)) + f_phi(rho_i(v))] for every n. Equivalently, the inequality holds for every f(rho) = int log(1+r rho) dmu(r) with mu >= 0, a subclass of concave increasing functions vanishing at 0.

Step 3 (this page). Take phi(r) = r^{-p} with 0<p<1. The substitution r = s/rho gives f_phi(rho) = rho^p int_0^inf s^{-p}/(1+s) ds = (pi/sin(p pi)) rho^p. Hence, with S_p^{(n)}(u) = sum_{i<=n} rho_i(u)^p:
- S_p^{(n)}(u+v) <= S_p^{(n)}(u) + S_p^{(n)}(v) for all n;
- letting n go to infinity, S_p(u+v) <= S_p(u) + S_p(v).
This is the p-triangle inequality, so the class of operators with sum rho_i^p < infinity (0<p<1) is a p-normed (quasi-Banach) space. The 'Remarque' adds that this sharpens Weyl's inequality (Weyl 1949).

Step 4 (the 'Question'). Grothendieck asks to characterize all functions f of a positive variable such that f^{(n)}(u) = sum_{i<=n} f(rho_i(u)) satisfies f^{(n)}(u+v) <= f^{(n)}(u) + f^{(n)}(v) for all n, and u, v in L(E) arbitrary. He notes that the case n = infinity may suffice, and proposes a generalization to functions of n arguments, i.e. symmetric gauge-type functions of the whole singular sequence.

Purpose: build the quasi-normed ideals of operators with p-summable singular values or eigenvalues (p<1), needed for his Fredholm theory and the order of Fredholm determinants. The next page proves the bound ||u_1 ^ ... ^ u_n||_1 <= (1/n!) prod ||u_i||_1 and Tr(Lambda^n u) = alpha_n(u).
errors: The constant is int_0^inf s^{-p}/(1+s) ds = pi/sin(p pi), finite only for 0<p<1. The machine transcription's 's^{1/p}' should be 's^{-p}'.
The notation f_i(u) on this page must mean rho_i(u) (equivalently f(rho_i(u))); it is an abbreviation, not a new object.
Previous page: A'(r) should be sum rho_i/(1+r rho_i), not sum r/(1+r rho_i). This is a slip.

The base multiplicative inequality for the rho_i of a sum is not proved here. It holds for Hilbert-space singular numbers (Horn-Fan type); its validity for whatever Banach-space rho_i is meant depends on their definition, which this page does not show.

The integration-by-parts step needs phi(r)A(r) to vanish at infinity, or a truncation. For phi = r^{-p} and A(r) ~ n log r this holds; the boundary term at 0 uses A(0)=0. These are minor technical gaps, adequately sketched.

ideas.what: Subadditivity of partial sums of p-th powers of singular numbers: sum_{i<=n} s_i(u+v)^p <= sum_{i<=n} s_i(u)^p + sum_{i<=n} s_i(v)^p for 0<p<1. Hence the Schatten-type class S_p (p<1) is p-normed.
ideas.modern_name: Rotfel'd inequality / p-triangle inequality for Schatten quasi-norms (0<p<1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Ju. Rotfel'd (1967-69); C. A. McCarthy, 'c_p' (1967); also in Gohberg-Krein's book
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Produits tensoriels topologiques (Mem. AMS 16, 1955) or La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956) in connection with p-summable operators; unsure whether this precise inequality is stated there.

ideas.what: Method: from the multiplicative inequality for prod(1+r s_i) obtain additive inequalities for all f(rho) = int phi(r) rho/(1+r rho) dr with phi decreasing, i.e. f = int log(1+r rho) dmu(r). This is integration by parts against a decreasing kernel, a majorization-type argument.
ideas.modern_name: Integral representation of concave (Bernstein/Stieltjes-type) functions combined with weak (log-)majorization; essentially Rotfel'd's proof technique
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rotfel'd (1969); Thompson (1976); Bourin-Uchiyama (2007) for general concave f

ideas.what: Computation f_phi(rho) = c_p rho^p for phi = r^{-p}
ideas.modern_name: Mellin integral / Beta-function identity int_0^inf s^{-p}/(1+s) ds = pi/sin(p pi)

ideas.what: Question: characterize all f with sum_{i<=n} f(s_i(u+v)) <= sum_{i<=n} f(s_i(u)) + f(s_i(v)) for all n and all operators; extend to functions of n arguments.
ideas.modern_name: Characterization of functions/symmetric gauge functions subadditive on singular values (Rotfel'd-Thompson problem; Bourin-Uchiyama subadditivity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rotfel'd 1969 and R. C. Thompson 1976 (sufficiency of concavity with f(0)=0); Uchiyama, Bourin-Uchiyama 2007

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck proved the p-subadditivity sum s_i(u+v)^p <= sum s_i(u)^p + sum s_i(v)^p (0<p<1), including the stronger version for every partial sum n. He used essentially the same route later used by Rotfel'd: a multiplicative inequality for prod(1+r s_i), then integration against a decreasing kernel. The literature credits this to Rotfel'd and McCarthy (1967-69).
missed.quote: S_p^{(n)}(u+v) <= S_p^{(n)}(u) + S_p^{(n)}(v) en particulier S_p(u+v) <= S_p(u) + S_p(v)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/attribution point in operator-ideal theory: Schatten quasi-norms and the Rotfel'd trace inequality would have been in hand about 14 years earlier, in the context of Fredholm determinants.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly posed the characterization problem for functions f making sum_{i<=n} f(s_i) subadditive for all n, and its multivariable (gauge-function) generalization. The sufficiency of concavity was settled by Rotfel'd/Thompson. Whether an exact characterization (necessary and sufficient) for the 'all n' version, or the multivariable version, is fully recorded in the literature is unclear.
missed.quote: Question : ... les fonctions f d'une variable positive telles que ... f^{(n)}(u+v) <= f^{(n)}(u)+f^{(n)}(v) quel que soit n ... Généralisation à des fonctions de n arguments.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The problem is still a natural one in matrix analysis (concave/subadditive functions of singular values). It is mostly resolved, but the exact necessary conditions are a residual question.

deep.surprise_reason: The p-triangle inequality for singular values with p<1, with a Rotfel'd-type integral-representation proof and an explicit question anticipating Rotfel'd/Thompson, is dated here to 1953, well before the credited sources (1967-1976). It is a nice unpublished priority detail, but the mathematics itself is now standard and Grothendieck may have used the consequence (p-normed ideals) in his published Fredholm work.

S_p^{(n)}(u) = sum_1^n rho_i(u)^p (the 'f_i(u)' stands for rho_i(u)).
Previous page: A'(r) = sum rho_i(u)/(1+r rho_i(u)).
Illegible remark lines plausibly read: '... ce qui est plus précis que l'inégalité de Weyl; on trouve ...', i.e. a comparison with Weyl's inequalities.
